steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease baking sheets.

Beat together butter, sugar, and vanilla in a large bowl with an electric mixer until creamy and well combined. Mix in flour a little at a time until incorporated. Gently fold in potato chips. Drop dough by spoonfuls onto the prepared baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until the edges are golden brown, about 15 minutes. Transfer cookies to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: My Grandmother's Potato Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These easy potato chip cookies are irresistible, have a lovely crunch, and use just 5 simple ingredients to make a sweet and salty eggless treat.
raw_recipe.name: My Grandmother's Potato Chip Cookies

review.reviewBody: The first batch I left in balls as they dropped off the spoon and they were a little "doughy" in the center. The second batch I flattened and baked at the reccommended time. The 3rd batch I flattened and then forgot about when I got a phone call! It turned out WAY better. They were in for almost 25 min. and golden brown around the edges. Fantastic!

This is a wonderful recipe that is easy to make. The taste reminds me of a buttery shortbread. Simple in favor and the texture is like none other, can't even describe it but it's very pleasing. I used Lay's Potato Chips and baked them for 18 minutes. Delicious! I've got to believe that the two who scored this recipe low must not have followed the directions correctly. It says 2 cups of butter not 2 sticks and that may have been the problem with the first review. The second review said she put the dough in the fridge before baking even though the recipe doesn't call for that action. Anyway, follow the instructions as written except bake until desired doneness. I baked some of mine on a greased cookie sheet and the rest on a parchment lined cookie sheet with similar results. The parchment ones were a little less greasy on the bottom.
Love this cookie! I used brown sugar. Did not crush potato chips very fine and baked for 15 minutes at 375. I flattened. the cookies before baking. Turned out nice and crispy. Toots
Love this cookie! I used brown sugar. Did not crush potato chips very fine and baked for 15 minutes at 375. I flattened. the cookies before baking. Turned out nice and crispy. Toots
I also added 1- Cup of toasted ground pecans to the batter. This gave the cookies a more rounded flavor complex. This has been a favorite since childhood!😍
Always a hit wherever I take these cookies! I add mini chocolate chips. I also flatten them down before baking.

These were the perfect combination of salty and sweet! They have a lovely butter flavor and shortbread texture. I made a half batch because I didn't want to use up all of my butter and I kinda regret it. 

I substituted brown sugar because that's what I had. I flattened tablespoon balls of dough and sprinkled with crushed chips before putting them in the oven. Once they were out, I sprinkled some flaky sea salt on top. 

These only lose a star because they don't have any chocolate which would totally elevate these to perfect cookie status.

I make these cookies every Christmas. I have added a twist though that my children just love....after the cookies have cooled, I dip half of each cookie in melted dark chocolate and additional crushed up potato chips. They are a true crowd pleaser! :)
People loved them, from Washington State to Arizona! Quality chips make a quality cookie! Wavy lays were the chosen chip and chip eaters could pick the brand and type!
I’ve been this recipe for years! My grandma made them all the time. I add a little almond extract and drizzle cooled cookies with melted chocolate wafers. Works best with cheap salty chips.
I live in altitude. Read the reviews first. Flattened them a little, baked for 20 min. Perfect! Now, if only chocolate chip cookies would come out this well….
Great taste. Easy to make. Get to use those darn broken potato chips. No more waste.
I added, diced up macadamia nuts and diced up white chocolate chips to mine
Perfect! We loved them!! So easy to make!
I brought these cookies into the office. I could hear the staff members raving about them. It made my day. So easy and a good use of the bottom of the bag chip pieces! Enjoy!!

This recipe is fool proof. If you didn’t like the cookie blame the chef. For those complaining about the lack of sweetness. Sprinkle some powered sugar on them lightly and/or some green or red sugar. These cookies are the best when made smaller.
Dropped spoonfuls on to prepared baking sheets (I buttered mine). Baked at 350 degrees for 15 minutes. Came out perfectly! Tasted every bit as delicious as I remember from my childhood. 🥰
Horrible recipe, cookies looked as though they hadn't even been baked. Seems as though ingredients have been left out of grandmother's recipe. Save yourself the aggravation, keep looking....
